docSummary: Agency X (synthetic fixture) is scoping a managed AMS engagement covering 12 eServices (one, Booklet, being decommissioned), currently run by an incumbent team of 30-36 people, with L1 handled by the agency's own help desk and an intermediate L1.5 team (3-4 people) filtering 20-30% of tickets before L2/L3. The FY25 table (Apr-2025 to Mar-2026, a 12-month period) shows totals of 3066 SRs, 636 severity-rated incidents (155 Sev A→P1, 474 Sev B→P2, 7 Sev C→P3), and 202 CRs; these were divided by 12 to get monthly figures (SR≈255.5/mo, CR≈16.83/mo, inc≈53.0/mo). Job-failure counts (92 total across eServices) were excluded from incidents since the document does not say they are logged as incidents. Two separate automation initiatives (account-review collation and weekly log analysis) were captured as opportunities, not as part of the AMS tower. Hosting/infrastructure (public cloud, Singapore region) is run by a separate hosting vendor and security incidents by a separate enterprise team, so no IMS tower was created.

towers.label: eServices application support, combined AMS (12 eServices: Portal, Callup, Manning, Deferment, Payslip, Registration, Clearance, Pay, Awards, Leave and Claims, Retail, Posting - Booklet decommissioning)

opportunities.name: Account Review Automation
opportunities.note: ~12 man-days/month manually collating ~5,000 accounts/month into Excel with no central database and no audit trail; scope later revised from 10 systems to 12 sources across 5 categories; standalone 2-month tool proposed, modular for future AIOps integration.

opportunities.name: Log Analysis Automation
opportunities.note: Weekly manual review of 5 log use cases by one person using an email/Excel workflow; candidate to plug into a future AIOps pipeline.

warnings: Job-failure counts (total 92 over FY25: Pay 30, Awards 8, Retail 54, Posting 0) are operational counters, not described as logged incidents, so they were excluded from inc/mix - verify if they should be included.
Callup shows 140 Sev A incidents against only 80 SRs for that eService - an unusual ratio; flagged by the bid team's own analysis too, but extracted as stated.

An earlier session reported platform-wide Sev A as 6 for FY25; the session-4 table shows Sev A total of 155 (Callup 140 + Manning 15). Used the later, more detailed table value and treated the earlier figure as superseded.

Session 3 states 12 eServices total with Booklet being decommissioned (implying 11 active), but the session-4 table lists 12 named eServices with no Booklet row - the counts don't reconcile; please check.
Account-review scope changed between sessions (10 systems -> 12 sources across 5 categories); latest figure used in the opportunity note, not sized as a tower.

An L1.5 team (3-4 people, client-run, 24x7) filters 20-30% of tickets before L2; per instructions this intermediate team's rate is excluded from pass12/pass23, and pass12 was omitted since L1 is out of the bidder's scope.
pass23 was derived from 'less than 5% are handled at L3' - used 5% as an upper-bound estimate, not an exact observed rate.
Incumbent FTE of 33 is the midpoint of a stated 30-36 person range.
A separate platform team of 18 FTE exists but is explicitly a separate tender - excluded from incumbentFTE and towers.

'Fewer than 1000 users are supported' and '4000 concurrent users at maximum' appear to describe different populations (admin/internal vs. public-facing) - not reconciled, and neither was used as a mau figure since the tower is sized in history mode.
Hosting/infrastructure (public cloud, Singapore region) is run by a separate hosting vendor and security incidents by a separate enterprise team - neither was treated as an IMS tower for the bidder.
L2/L3 ownership ('us') is inferred from context (incumbent team being replaced) - the document does not explicitly state who will run L2/L3 under the new contract.
eng.region/locMix omitted - the only location mentioned (public cloud hosting in Singapore) describes hosting, not the bidder's delivery team location.
CR complexity mix (srMix equivalent for CRs) was not stated with enough structure to populate crMix, so it was omitted.
Page 5 contains an AI-generated bid-team analysis (indicative pods/FTE) explicitly marked as not client-stated; none of its figures were used.
